report_name: China-Aligned Group TA419 Targets U.S. AI Policy Experts

threat_actors.name: TA419
threat_actors.description: A China-aligned cyber-espionage group conducting sophisticated phishing campaigns targeting U.S. experts in artificial intelligence policy to steal cloud credentials and gather intelligence.
threat_actors.goals: Gather intelligence on U.S. AI strategy, policy formulation, and private sector developments.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: TA419 sends emails containing a shortened URL that directs victims to a convincing adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing portal.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor uses adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing sites, such as those built with the Frameless BitB framework, to proxy the connection to legitimate services like Microsoft 365, allowing the real-time capture of credentials and MFA tokens.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The AitM phishing setup allows TA419 to steal the user's authenticated session cookie, enabling them to bypass MFA and hijack the session to access the victim's cloud account.

attack_patterns.name: Impersonation
attack_patterns.description: TA419 impersonates prominent individuals, including former White House officials, economists, and senior employees from the AI company Anthropic, to build rapport and lend credibility to their phishing attempts.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The ultimate goal of the campaign is to steal valid Microsoft 365 / Entra ID credentials to gain access to cloud accounts for intelligence gathering.

tools.name: Frameless BitB
tools.description: Used as a framework to create convincing adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing portals that impersonate legitimate Microsoft login pages.

identities.name: U.S. AI Policy Experts
identities.description: A class of individuals in the United States targeted by TA419, including people at think tanks, universities, and legal firms specializing in AI policy.

identities.name: Anthropic
identities.description: An AI company whose senior employees were impersonated by TA419 in phishing emails to lend credibility to their social engineering efforts.

infrastructure.name: TA419 AitM Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing portals designed to impersonate Microsoft login pages and harvest credentials, MFA tokens, and session cookies. The infrastructure uses domains registered through providers like NameSilo.

infrastructure.name: TA419 C2 Backend Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Backend infrastructure used by TA419 for its phishing campaigns, which is masked using Cloudflare services.

indicators.name: Suspicious Entra ID Sign-in with Session Risk
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Entra ID Sign-in with Session Risk
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a successful Microsoft Entra ID sign-in where a session risk (such as anomalous token or unfamiliar location) was detected. This could indicate a compromised session, potentially following an adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing attack like those used by TA419 to steal session cookies.
references:
  - https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/hallucinating-credibility-china-aligned-ta419-impersonates-its-way-us-ai-policy
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-02
tags:
  - attack.t1539
  - attack.t1078.004
  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    ResultType: 0
    Status.errorCode: 0
    RiskLevelAggregated:
      - 'medium'
      - 'high'
    RiskLevelDuringSignIn:
      - 'medium'
      - 'high'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a successful Microsoft 365 / Entra ID sign-in where a session risk was identified, such as an anomalous token or unfamiliar location. This is indicative of a compromised session, a key goal of TA419's AitM attacks.
